business_problem: Siemens Gamesa needed to cut blade-manufacturing errors and reduce rework because manual inspection and a partially automated laser-grid system could not deliver the precision, throughput, or standardization needed across expanding factories.
solution_summary: Siemens Gamesa and IBM Consulting turned a visual quality-control concept into a production-ready computer-vision system for turbine-blade manufacturing. IBM helped the Digital Ventures Lab design a camera array above each manufacturing station, process video on Microsoft Azure IoT Edge, and apply machine-learning models in real time so the laser grid system could validate fiberglass placement and later detect foreign objects in the mold. Microsoft Azure Machine Learning and Azure DevOps supported the cloud engineering and model lifecycle, while IBM Garage methodology accelerated iterative delivery from design to MVP in Aalborg. The architecture kept feedback close to the production line: images are analyzed with minimal latency at the edge, then the resulting guidance is projected back into the manufacturing process so technicians can act immediately. By standardizing the digital workflow on Azure and scaling it plant by plant, Siemens Gamesa created a reusable manufacturing-intelligence platform rather than a one-off inspection tool.

data_flow: Cameras mounted above the blade stations capture video, Azure IoT Edge runs machine-learning inference on the footage, the laser-grid system returns placement guidance and defect alerts to technicians, and Azure services manage the broader model and delivery lifecycle.
integration_points: production lines in Aalborg, Le Havre, and Hull
business_outcome: Siemens Gamesa reduced rework risk, improved manufacturing consistency, and created a faster path for scaling best practices across new and existing turbine-blade factories.
metrics: payback period of about two and a half years
architecture_clues: A distributed camera array and edge-computing stack were chosen instead of a smaller number of high-resolution cameras.
Video is processed at the edge so feedback can be returned to technicians in real time.
The platform is designed to be replicated across multiple factories and new lines.
